fields.meta_title: Forklift Inspection Form Builder With Alerts | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a forklift inspection form operators fill in before each shift, with defect alerts, battery checks, and a repair sign-off. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Forklift Inspection Form That Routes Every Defect
fields.hero_description: Build a forklift inspection form that logs each pre-shift check and sends any failed item to maintenance.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Records and Where a Fail Goes
fields.features_subheading: Operators see a short checklist on a phone. The six parts below cover what sits behind it once they press submit.
fields.feature_1:
Checks written for your trucks

Emergent builds the form from a plain-English description of your fleet, such as battery checks for electric trucks. Ask for a new item later and Emergent adds it to the form.
fields.feature_2:
Pass or fail, with a note on a fail

The operator marks every item on the list pass or fail. A fail opens a note field where the operator writes what they saw, such as a brake pedal that sinks almost to the floor.
fields.feature_3:
Failed items reach maintenance

The form sends the truck number and the operator's note to the maintenance contact you name, in Slack or by email. Name a backup as well for any fails found on the night shift.
fields.feature_4:
A live board of this shift's checks

The dashboard updates as each check is submitted. A shift lead can see at a glance which trucks are cleared to run and which ones still have no check logged against them.
fields.feature_5:
Every check in a database you own

Each submission is stored with the truck number, the operator, and the time. Emergent sets no cap on responses, even for a large fleet checked after every single shift.
fields.feature_6:
One question per screen

Operators can step through the checklist one item at a time on a phone. Each screen holds one check with its pass and fail buttons, and nothing else on it to scroll past.

fields.usecase_heading: What a Forklift Check Sets in Motion
fields.tab_content_1:
Truck 4 fails its brake check and comes off the floor

Odell Rasmussen starts his shift at Quarrytown Logistics by checking Truck 4 on his phone. At 6:10 am he marks the service brake as a fail and notes that the pedal sinks. The form sets Truck 4 to out of service, and maintenance lead Colette Dumont gets a Slack direct message with his note.
fields.tab_content_2:
No check 30 minutes into a shift means a reminder

Yarrowby Cold Storage runs its 12 trucks around the clock and checks each one after every shift. At 2:30 pm, 30 minutes into the second shift, the board showed 11 of 12 trucks checked. Truck 9 had no check yet, and its operator, Pavel Brannagh, got a Slack reminder to do it before lifting a load.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any battery reading under 30% sends its truck to charge

Sallow Creek Distribution runs an electric fleet, and its operators log battery charge and electrolyte level before each shift. This morning Truck E-6 came in under 30%. The form sent it to the charging area instead of the dock, and shift lead Junie Pascoe got an email naming the truck.
fields.tab_content_4:
Trucks come back after a mechanic signs the repair

A truck that fails a check at Brixham Lumber stays out of service until its repair is signed. On Monday an operator failed Truck 2 for a worn mast chain. Mechanic Rurik Vasko replaced the chain on Tuesday and signed the repair on a tablet, and only then did Truck 2 show as back in service.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Forklift Inspection Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these steps to set up a forklift inspection form that operators finish before each shift and that routes failed items to maintenance.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide what a failed item does
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each truck's number and its power type, electric or propane. Give each power type its own checklist and keep the battery checks on the electric one only.
fields.howto_step_2_des: OSHA publishes sample daily checklists for powered industrial trucks on its website. Copy the items for your truck type, then add what your own trucks carry, such as a clamp attachment.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose which fails take a truck out of service and who hears about each one. A failed brake goes to the maintenance lead at once; a torn seat cover can wait for the weekly review.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Make the check due before each truck's first use of the day. If your trucks run round the clock, OSHA's rule calls for an examination after each shift: set a due time for every shift change.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your checklist and your fail rules into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form with its truck statuses and alerts. Change any part later by asking for it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit a test check with the service brake marked as a fail. Confirm the truck shows out of service and that the maintenance lead gets the message before operators see the form.
fields.howto_step_7_des: If your maintenance team works from a system with an API, connect the form to it. A failed item can then open a work order there as well as send the Slack message.

faq_plan.q: What is a forklift inspection form?
faq_plan.a: A forklift inspection form is the record an operator fills in while checking a forklift before driving it. Each item on the list is marked pass or fail, next to the truck number, the operator's name, and the time of the check. A finished form shows that the truck was looked at that day and what the operator found.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a forklift inspection form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: your truck numbers, the items for each power type, and who hears about a fail. Emergent builds the form from that description and changes it when you ask, for example to add a mirror check to one truck.

faq_plan.q: How often do operators use a daily forklift inspection form?
faq_plan.a: At least once a day for each truck in use: OSHA's forklift rule says the examination "shall be made at least daily." Tie each form to a truck number instead of a person. A truck shared by two operators then shows one check for the day, and a truck nobody checked shows none.

faq_plan.q: Can I build a daily forklift inspection form free?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing a daily forklift inspection form. Keep that form about the truck itself: how well someone drives belongs on a separate employee evaluation form, not on the truck's record.

faq_plan.q: What should an electric forklift inspection form include?
faq_plan.a: Battery checks, on top of the items every truck gets. OSHA's sample checklist for electric trucks has the operator check the battery's water and electrolyte level and its charge. Record the charge as a percentage instead of a tick, since a number is what lets a low reading set off a rule.

faq_plan.q: Can I use a forklift annual inspection form instead of daily checks?
faq_plan.a: No. A yearly inspection sits alongside the daily checks, which OSHA's rule sets at a minimum of once a day. File the annual form against the same truck number as the daily ones, and the truck's record shows both side by side.

faq_plan.q: Should a forklift inspection checklist form include who fixed each problem?
faq_plan.a: Yes. OSHA's sample daily checklists tell operators to "Have a qualified mechanic correct all problems," and a line for the mechanic's name shows who did. Ask operators to report the fault and leave the repair to the mechanic. If the same fault keeps turning up, cover it in the next operator training and ask about it on a training feedback form afterward.

faq_plan.q: When do you use a forklift pre trip inspection form?
faq_plan.a: Before the truck goes into service. OSHA's rule says trucks "shall be examined before being placed in service." If that examination shows a condition "adversely affecting the safety of the vehicle," the truck stays out of service. Have operators submit the form before they lift their first load.

faq_plan.q: What should a forklift pre use inspection form record besides pass or fail?
faq_plan.a: The truck number, the operator, the time, and the hour meter reading. The hour meter reading gives the mechanic the truck's working hours at each check. The form saves every submission in a database you own, and Emergent puts no cap on how many checks you collect.

faq_plan.q: What should a forklift safety inspection form include for defects?
faq_plan.a: A way to mark the truck out of service, and a record of who was told about the defect. Under OSHA's rule, a truck that is "not in safe operating condition" is removed from service. The rule also says defects are to be "immediately reported and corrected" once found. Name a backup for days the maintenance lead is away, such as a day off approved on a time off request form.

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable checklists: city and university PDFs, OSHA's sample daily checklists, a J.J. Keller shop page and an Etsy listing. Each gives an operator a sheet to tick and stops there. This page shows what a forklift inspection form does once the operator submits it, in four places a safety or warehouse lead will recognize: a failed service brake that takes Truck 4 out of service and messages the maintenance lead, a round-the-clock cold store where a truck with no check 30 minutes into the shift gets its operator a reminder, an electric fleet where a battery under 30% goes to the charging area, and a lumber yard where a mechanic signs off a repair before the truck returns. The FAQ covers the definition, daily, pre-use and pre-trip timing from the OSHA rule, electric and annual forms, and what happens to a defect.
